subject: Post-demo: TiltProducts model-fit recommendations & schema plan
body:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Greene <alex.greene@tiltproducts.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Jan 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: TiltProducts model-fit recommendations & schema plan

Hi Alex / Sara —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap + recommended next steps so we have alignment before the eval run. Appreciate you looping procurement if we move to a pilot (cc'd the likely internal contacts).

Recap of what we saw:
- Demo covered product use-case: invoice data extraction + business-rule tagging (structured JSON outputs + lookup calls).
- Primary constraints: strict schema conformance, occasional numeric rounding rules, and need for deterministic retries/fallback when tool-calls fail.
- Success metrics you emphasized: 98% schema-valid output, <200ms median token-latency for short prompts, and <1% silent schema-failure rate on pilot load.

Recommended model candidates for the eval (starting point):
1) redwood-bonsai-7b (default): best mix of latency, deterministic structured output handling, and tool-calling hooks.
2) open-stablelm-3b-q5 (low-cost variant): useful for burst/overflow paths; will need quantization testing for numeric precision.

Suggested eval scope (3 working days):
- Run the same prompt set across both models with function/tool-calls enabled.
- Evaluate JSON schema validation (strict) and record failures, partial outputs, and repaired outputs.
- Track per-request: model, prompt id, tokens, latency, schema_result (valid|invalid|partial), and any tool-call errors.

Attached: prompt_set_v1.jsonl (shortest 120 prompts covering edge cases) and benchmark_run_summary.csv (initial perf numbers from demo).

Key questions / asks from us:
- Can you provide a list of the top 5 schema variants we need to support? (example: invoice_v1, invoice_v1_lineitems_expanded, supplier_contact_minimal, etc.)
- Are there any IP/data residency constraints for payloads in the pilot?

Next steps (proposed):
1) I'll spin up a 3-day eval config and share the run link + dashboard (we'll provide a small test token).
2) You confirm the schema variants and sample files (or tell us we can use the ones in prompt_set_v1).
3) If results look good, we schedule a short pilot planning call next week to discuss procurement/terms.

Thanks —
Monica

Subject: Re: Post-demo: TiltProducts model-fit recommendations & schema plan

Hi Monica —

Appreciate the write-up. A couple quick clarifications before we start the run: 

1) Schema enforcement: do you validate the model response post-hoc (on the server side) only, or can the model be configured to strictly follow the JSON schema and return a machine-validated object? Our parsing layer is brittle and we'd prefer outputs that are JSON-first.

2) Retries & fallback: if a tool call (e.g., external price lookup) fails mid-conversation, what's your recommended retry strategy? We want to avoid duplicate external requests on retries and keep eventual consistency for downstream systems.

3) Cost / model mapping: for long-term ops, is there an easy way to route high-SLO traffic to the bonsai model and low-cost bulk processing to the stablelm variant?

Also cc'd procurement (sara) to flag they'll need an initial statement-of-work if we proceed.

—Alex
Alex Greene
Head of Product Integrations, TiltProducts
alex.greene@tiltproducts.com

On Sat, 24 Jan 2026 at 11:04, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Adding a quick technical note — we can do strict server-side JSON validation and return a structured error with an HTTP 422 when invalid. For stricter model-level compliance we recommend using a JSON schema in the prompt + schema enforcement plug-in we include in the eval harness; that reduces free-text deviations by ~75% in our internal benchmarks.
>
> -Karthik

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Greene <alex.greene@tiltproducts.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Jan 2026 09:00:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: TiltProducts model-fit recommendations & schema plan

Thanks Alex — good questions. Short answers + plan below (see proposed eval details).

1) JSON schema enforcement:
- We perform server-side validation by default and return structured validation errors.
- For the eval, we'll enable our \"schema hinting\" layer in the prompt (calls out required types/enum sets and an explicit JSON wrapper). That combined approach gives the highest practical compliance with minimal model engineering.
- If you require 100% pre-validated outputs, we can add a verify/fix step: when validation fails, our harness runs a constrained re-write prompt to correct the output; we log both tries and whether the repair passed validation.

2) Retries & tool-calls:
- Recommended default: exponential backoff with idempotency tokens. The eval harness will attach a request_id to each external lookup and our middleware de-duplicates identical request_ids on retries.
- Fallback behavior: if after N retries (configurable, default 3) the lookup still fails, we surface a clear error object in the JSON (\"external_lookup_status\":\"failed\", \"reason\":...) so downstream systems can decide — rather than silently returning partial data.

3) Routing by SLO/cost:
- Yes — routing policies in the console can send traffic by tag (e.g., production-high-slo -> bonsai-7b; batch-processing -> stablelm-3b-q5). We can provide a draft policy you can apply.

Proposed eval config (we will provision):
- 3 days, 1k prompts/day across the two model candidates.
- Schema enforcement enabled + retry logging.
- Aggregated dashboard with per-prompt schema pass/fail, latency percentile, and repair effectiveness.

Deliverables if you approve:
- Eval dashboard link and CSV export.
- Short one-page summary with recommended quantization and batch settings for pilot.

If that sounds good, I can start the run tomorrow and share access.

Monica

Quick follow from my side — added a few engineering constraints and a suggested test plan we can attach to the eval: 

- Quantization notes: for the stablelm-3b-q5 path, test q5_0 first; avoid aggressive q3/Q2 for money fields as we saw precision drift in earlier runs.
- Batching: use sequence-length-aware batching; set max_batch to 16 for 1-2s token lengths to preserve latency SLOs.
- Schema test plan: we'll run schema fuzzing (mutations of required fields) and check repair-success-rate; see attached schema_test_plan.md.

Action items for next week:
1) Monica: start the eval run and share the dashboard link + temp API key.
2) Alex / Sara: confirm the set of schema variants we should include (or give us a sample dataset).
3) Marissa: please prepare a 1-page pilot recommendation (pricing tiers + routing policy) we can share with procurement.

Karthik
